A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIT research, with matching methods and original evaluations. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated in v4.

before.justification: v1 reports original hidden-topic recovery, news-summary reconstruction, rank and trigger generalization, cross-behavior transfer, and trigger-recovery experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds adaptive-agent comparisons, adapter-rank ablations, OOD data-scaling experiments, and evaluation-metric analyses.

M1.justification: The synthetic labeled-weight-diff training scheme, supervised objective, LoRA interpreter, and inference procedure are retained. Appendix E relocates the original method motivation. Varying interpreter rank is an experimental ablation, not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic hidden-topic and news-summary tasks, including the existing zero-width-space trigger scenarios. The added experiments vary comparators, adapter configurations, training-set sizes, and scoring within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.6 adds a GPT-5.1 adaptive probing agent and its trigger-informed oracle variant to the hidden-topic comparison. Unlike the retained fixed-question baselines, this agent queries both original and finetuned models and chooses subsequent questions interactively. Figures C.3–C.4 report its evaluated performance.

E3.justification: New protocols include agent budgets of 20 queries and 100 for Qwen3-4B, DIT-adapter ranks from 1 to 128, and OOD training-data scaling with fixed training steps. Appendix K adds text-embedding-3-small cosine similarity, min-max scaled to 1–5. The original splits and primary LLM-judge evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds interpreter-rank sensitivity, OOD data-scaling analysis, agent query-budget sensitivity, and metric robustness with individual scoring disagreements. These address new questions beyond v1's retained inspected-weight-rank sweep, in-distribution data scaling, and generalization tests.

E5.justification: The original score-distribution tables and error-barred figures are retained. Additional plots do not establish a new uncertainty-reporting practice, and v4 adds no explicit repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval methodology, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v1 Tables F.1–F.6 retain their numerical results as v4 Tables G.1–G.6. Substantial new findings include weak agent recovery even with 100 queries, limited gains beyond adapter rank 16, improving OOD recovery with more training data, and preserved advantages over non-oracle probes under embedding scoring. Table K.2 adds concrete scoring disagreements.

T1.justification: WEIGHTDIFFQA renames the existing problem without changing its mathematical content. The training losses, adapter-commutativity argument, and parallel-LoRA formula are retained; Equation 3 moves to Appendix E. No substantive formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain DIT and its two proof-of-concept demonstrations, including rank generalization. v4 foregrounds failed cross-behavior transfer in the introduction, but this limitation was already established in v1 Section 6.1. The added evidence does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 adds architectural limitations involving unavailable original-model internals and possible adapter interference, plus proposed reasoning-based training. New appendices interpret capacity saturation, data scaling, agent failures, and lexical versus conceptual scoring biases. Appendix H also adds broader mechanistic and generalization interpretations to the retained weight visualizations.

D1.justification: v4 adds training-data and agent-transcript access links, the agent's versioned model identifier and query interface, and monetary compute estimates with pricing assumptions and data-generation costs. Existing code and weight links, training times, hardware, and core implementation descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds substantive positioning relative to model diffing, including sparse crosscoders, stage-wise dictionary updates, and mechanistic finetuning studies. It also addresses privileged-information critiques of activation verbalization and connects the work to latent-knowledge elicitation. Appendix H adds supporting finetuning and representation literature.

P1.justification: v4 standardizes WEIGHTDIFFQA and DIT-adapter terminology, edits existing prose, and relocates method motivation and mechanistic visualization discussion to Appendices E and H. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 revises Figure 3.1, adds agent, rank, scaling, and metric-comparison figures plus Table K.2, and adds cost columns to the compute tables. Figure K.1 partly redisplays the original evaluation. Weight visualizations are relocated and reordered, and the ICLR layout changes figure sizing and placement throughout.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens empirical validation beyond v1's fixed-question comparisons and single scoring approach. The adaptive-agent evaluation and alternative-metric check address important weaknesses in assessing DIT's advantage, while rank and controlled data-scaling analyses test explanations for its performance. Added resource information and research positioning further improve assessability. Applicability remains limited by synthetic tasks and failed cross-behavior transfer, and some mechanistic interpretations remain speculative, but these limits do not outweigh the validation gains.
